newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 1st-qtr current account surplus US$1.928 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 1st-qtr current account surplus US$1.928 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's first-quarter current account balance was a surplus of US$1.928 billion, down from a revised year-earlier surplus of US$2.024 billion, the central bank said on Tuesday.
The first-quarter surplus was significantly higher than an average forecast for a surplus of US$1.045 billion compiled from a May 19 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
The first-quarter surplus was well below that of the previous quarter, when Taiwan's current account balance posted a surplus of US$2.757 billion.

Central bank officials revised the first-quarter 1996 balance to a surplus of US$2.024 billion from US$1.793 billion, saying economists had adjusted their calculations to be more in line with International Monetary Fund practices.

Broken down into its main components, the first-quarter current account showed a merchandise surplus of US$3.097 billion compared with a US$3.483 billion surplus in the 1996 quarter.
The income component showed a quarterly surplus of US$992 million compared to a year-earlier surplus of US$1.343 billion.
The services component showed a first-quarter deficit of US$1.774 billion compared to US$2.210 billion year-earlier deficit.

A central bank statement attributed to the decline in the merchandise surplus to a higher rate of import growth compared to export growth. This reflected an import rise driven by Taiwan's general economic recovery as well as rising payments against surging deliveries of foreign military equipment.
In recent years, Taiwan generally has shown a surplus in merchandise and income, but a deficit in services.

Reuters Poll economists had said a 28.3 percent year-on-year decline in Taiwan's first-quarter trade surplus to US$1.817 billion should contribute to a lower first-quarter current account surplus compared to the year-earlier level.
The central bank said Taiwan's capital account balance in the first quarter showed a deficit of US$74 million compared to a first-quarter 1996 deficit of US$327 million.
The decline mainly reflected lower remittances of capital to Taiwan people who have emigrated overseas, the bank said.

Taiwan's first-quarter financial account showed a net inflow of US$831 million, with Taiwan investment overseas showing a net outflow of US$966 million compared with an outflow of US$945 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Foreign investment in Taiwan showed an inflow of US$287 million compared with a year-earlier inflow of US$187 million.
The central bank said its overseas assets had increased US$3.074 billion.
